title: The Appeal of Slow Travel
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
passage:
Slow travel, (1)___ unlike its fast-paced counterpart, places far greater emphasis on the journey (2)___ than the destination. (3)___, increasing numbers of travellers choose to spend weeks, rather (4)___ days, in a single region, getting to know its language, cuisine and customs (5)___ depth.

Proponents argue that this approach not only reduces the carbon footprint that comes (6)___ frequent short flights but also leads (7)___ a far richer, more meaningful experience overall. (8)___ said, slow travel is not without its critics, who point out that it is, in practice, a luxury available only to those with the time and money to spare.

questions.explanation: 'Quite unlike' means 'very different from'. It softens/intensifies the contrast being drawn with fast-paced travel.
The fixed pattern 'A rather than B' contrasts the journey itself with the destination.
A linking adverb is needed to show that the following clause is a result of the idea in the previous sentence.
'Rather than' is a fixed comparative structure: 'weeks, rather than days'.
'In depth' is a fixed phrase meaning thoroughly.
'Comes with' means 'is associated with' or 'results from'.
'Lead to' is a fixed verb + preposition combination meaning 'result in'.
'That said' is a fixed concessive phrase meaning 'however' or 'nevertheless'.
